_about: Questions with known-correct chunks, for scripts/measure_retrieval.py.
Committed so the measurement is repeatable: a hit rate is only comparable against itself if
the questions and the expected answers did not move between runs. A chunk is identified by
(source, heading), which is exactly what corpus.chunk_document writes into metadata -- not by
text, which would drift the moment a document was reworded.
Written the way someone actually asks, not as keyword echoes of the chunk. That distinction is
the whole point: HashingEmbeddings is term frequency over a fixed vocabulary, so a question
that reuses the section's own words is a question it cannot fail. Roughly half of these share
little or no vocabulary with their answer -- 'money back' for refund, 'tell the regulator' for
notification, 'looked at' for access, 'write-up' for written review. The `overlap` field says
which kind each one is, so a hit rate can be read per kind rather than as one average that

questions.question: How long do we keep authentication logs?
questions.heading: Retention periods
questions.note: 'authentication logs' appears verbatim; 'keep' vs 'retained' is the only gap.

questions.question: Who is allowed to declare an incident?
questions.heading: Declaration
questions.note: 'declare' and 'incident' both appear in the section.

questions.question: How quickly must we acknowledge a complaint?
questions.heading: Acknowledgement

questions.question: Which kind of complaint is growing fastest?
questions.heading: Common complaint categories

questions.question: What happens to data sitting in backups when someone asks to be deleted?
questions.heading: Backups
questions.note: 'backups' and 'deletion' appear; competes with 'Deletion on request', which is the near miss worth watching.

questions.question: Can a customer still get their money back after six weeks?
questions.heading: Eligibility window
questions.note: 'money back' for refund, 'six weeks' for thirty days. Nothing in the question appears in the answer except 'customer'.

questions.question: When do we have to tell the regulator about a data breach?
questions.heading: Regulator notification
questions.note: 'breach' appears nowhere in the corpus; the document says 'exposure of personal data'. 'regulator' is the only shared term.

questions.question: If a subscription was only half used, how much comes back?
questions.heading: Partial refunds
questions.note: 'half used' for partially consumed, 'how much comes back' for prorated refund.

questions.question: What is the deadline for the write-up after something goes wrong?
questions.heading: Post-incident review
questions.note: 'write-up' for written review, 'something goes wrong' for incident. No shared content words at all.

questions.question: Is there a record of who looked at a sensitive file?
questions.heading: Access logging
questions.note: 'looked at' for access, 'sensitive' for restricted, 'file' for record. The hardest one here.
